title: Acceptance probability after a fair choice
statement: Let $A$ be a machine with $m$ natural-number registers, control labels in $$, and instructions that may choose between two labels using a fair random bit; let $$ be an oracle, $x$ an input, and $G$ a guard on configurations. Suppose the instruction at label $l$ chooses between $l_1$ and $l_0$, and the configuration with label $l$, register values $v$, and no result satisfies $G$. If starting at $l_1$ with register values $v$ and no result terminates under $G$ with acceptance probability $p_1$, and starting at $l_0$ under the same conditions terminates under $G$ with acceptance probability $p_0$, then starting at $l$ terminates under $G$ with acceptance probability $(p_1+p_0)/2$.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at $l$ is a choice between $l_1$ and $l_0$.
The configuration $(l_1,v,	ext{no result})$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $p_1$.
The configuration $(l_0,v,	ext{no result})$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $p_0$.
caveat: The formal statement does not supply informal descriptions of the machine, oracle, guard, or probabilistic semantics; the statement characterizes these using their formal roles and the stated termination and acceptance properties.
